overall: The AG found the January 18, 2018 GIC Commission meeting notice violated the Open Meeting Law for lacking sufficient topic detail and using an unexplained acronym. No remedial order; the letter was issued as guidance because the contested vote was already rescinded.

allegations.summary: Notice topic 'Procurement: Medical/Behavioral Health Decision - VOTE' was too vague to tell the public the Commission would select and possibly eliminate health plan providers.
allegations.key_passage: did not convey clearly to members of the public or health plan members that the Commission would be selecting specific health plan providers

allegations.summary: Notice topics 'Public Hearings' and 'OOP Report' gave no detail on what would be discussed, and no specific matters subject to the hearings were identified.
allegations.key_passage: topics in the notice such as "Public Hearings" and "OOP Report" provide no detail or explanation so that a reasonable member of the public would understand what the Commission anticipates discussing

allegations.summary: The notice used the unexplained acronym 'OOP' (Out Of Pocket Report), which was not commonly understood.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission's notice did not identify any specific matters subject to a public hearing, nor did it explain what "OOP" means, though from the minutes we now understand this to mean Out Of Pocket Report.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
